title: Reading and spelling first words
audience: Adults relearning reading, for example after a brain injury
length_note: 11 short classes of 8 to 10 minutes each. Short classes are easier to focus on and easy to repeat. The course starts with whole words that matter in daily life (yes, no, help), so the learner has early wins and a reason to read. It then teaches letter sounds and sounding out three-letter words, one vowel group at a time so nothing is rushed. Spelling by choosing letters comes after the learner can read those words. Common sight words come last, followed by a class that puts words into short sentences. Each class can be repeated before moving on.

classes.title: Three important words: yes, no, help
classes.goal: Recognise and say yes, no and help when seen on their own, and pick each one from a small choice of words.
topics: Why whole words matter in daily life
Looking at the shape and letters of yes, no, help
Matching a word to a picture or meaning
Pick the word you hear from 2 or 3 choices

classes.title: Home words: water, home, TV
classes.goal: Recognise and say water, home and TV, and pick each one from a small choice of words.
topics: Reading water and home as whole words
TV as capital letters that stand for a word
Matching words to pictures
Mixed review with yes, no and help

classes.title: Letter sounds and joining them
classes.goal: Say the sound of common letters and blend two sounds into a short word such as at, up or in.
topics: Quick recap of letters from Letters A to Z
Letter sounds compared with letter names
Blending two sounds slowly, then faster
Reading at, in, up, on, am

classes.title: Sounding out three-letter words with A
classes.goal: Sound out and read simple three-letter words with the short A sound, such as cat, map, sad and hat.
topics: Three sounds, three taps: first, middle, last
Blending sound by sound into a word
Word families: cat, hat, mat, sat
Matching each word to a picture

classes.title: Sounding out words with I and O
classes.goal: Sound out and read three-letter words with short I and short O, such as sit, pin, dog and hot.
topics: The short I and short O sounds
Reading sit, pin, big, dog, hot, top
Telling A, I and O words apart
Review of A words

classes.title: Sounding out words with U and E
classes.goal: Sound out and read three-letter words with short U and short E, such as sun, cup, bed and pen.
topics: The short U and short E sounds
Reading sun, cup, bus, bed, pen, red
Mixed practice with all five vowels
Choosing the right word for a picture

classes.title: Spelling by choosing letters: everyday words
classes.goal: Spell yes, no, help and home by choosing letters in the right order from a set of letters.
topics: Spelling as choosing letters, not typing
Looking at a word, then choosing its letters in order
Fixing a wrong letter without worry
Spelling yes, no, help, home

classes.title: Spelling three-letter words by sound
classes.goal: Listen to a three-letter word, say its sounds, and choose the letters to spell it, for example cat, sit or sun.
topics: Say the word slowly and find each sound
Choosing the first, middle and last letter
Checking by sounding out what was spelled
Words with all five vowels

classes.title: Common sight words, set one
classes.goal: Recognise and read a first set of very common words at a glance, such as the, a, I, to, and, is.
topics: What sight words are and why they are worth knowing by sight
Reading the, a, I, to, and, is
Spotting them in short lines of text
Choosing their letters to spell them

classes.title: Common sight words, set two
classes.goal: Recognise and read a second set of common words at a glance, such as you, it, we, my, in, he and she.
topics: Reading you, it, we, my, in, he, she
Mixing set one and set two
Spotting them in short lines of text
Choosing their letters to spell some of them

classes.title: Putting words together: short sentences
classes.goal: Read short sentences such as 'I see the cat' and 'Help me' using sounding out and sight words.
topics: Reading left to right, one word at a time
Using sight words and sounding out together
Reading everyday sentences with yes, no, help, water, home
Choosing the missing word to finish a sentence
What to practise next
